article.Citation/Title: Johnson, M. W., Garcia-Romeu, A., & Griffiths, R. R. (2016). Long-term follow-up of psilocybin-facilitated smoking cessation. American Journal of Drug and Alcohol Abuse, 43(1), 55-60.
article.Outcome: 9/15 (60%) biologically verified (breath CO + urine cotinine + TLFB) smoking abstinence at long-term follow-up (mean 30 months post-TQD, range 16-57 months; single-arm, no comparator)
article.InterventionDescription: Oral psilocybin (20mg/70kg wk5, 30mg/70kg wk7, optional 30mg/70kg wk13) within 15-week CBT-based smoking-cessation program with mindfulness and guided imagery.

ae_events.Description: One participant reported decreased well-being/life satisfaction at 12-month follow-up, attributed to re-experiencing traumatic childhood memories during a psilocybin session; referred to counseling.

article.Citation/Title: This is a long-term follow-up report of a parent open-label pilot trial: Johnson MW, Garcia-Romeu A, Cosimano MP, Griffiths RR. 'Pilot study of the 5-HT2AR agonist psilocybin in the treatment of tobacco addiction.' J Psychopharmacol 2014;28(11):983-992 (ref. 4 in this article, cited repeatedly in Introduction/Methods as the source of the original sample, intervention description, and 6-month outcome data). The present article (Johnson 2016) reports previously unpublished 12-month and long-term (mean 30-month) follow-up data on the same 15 participants.
article.Outcome: Two abstinence timepoints are reported: 'At 12-month follow-up, 10 participants (67%) were confirmed as smoking abstinent. At long-term follow-up, nine participants (60%) were confirmed as smoking abstinent' (Abstract; Results). No statement anywhere designates one as the formal 'primary' outcome. I selected the long-term (mean 30-month, range 16-57 months post-TQD) rate of 9/15 (60%) as Outcome because it is the article's namesake/headline finding: the title is 'Long-term follow-up...', the Discussion's key comparative claim explicitly foregrounds it ('the present study found 60% abstinence more than a year after psilocybin administration', contrasted with <31% typical 12-month abstinence for standard medications), and the Conclusion cites 'long-term smoking abstinence' as the study's contribution. This is a judgment call — the abstract's Results sentence order technically states the 12-month figure (67%) first — and the alternative (12-month, 10/15) is a defensible substitute. Did not use the raw Figure 1 OCR chart-text block (garbled/interleaved axis labels) for any numeric value; only prose/table-reported numbers were used.
article.SD: No dispersion or test statistic is paired with either abstinence proportion; both are reported as raw counts/percentages with no accompanying inferential test (the reported ANOVA F and paired t-tests in Results/Fig.1 caption belong to the continuous TLFB cigarettes-per-day analysis, a different, non-primary measure, not to the abstinence-rate Outcome).
article.SampleSize_NFinal: Methods/Data analysis: 'Participants who did not report to a follow-up visit were considered to have smoked. The three participants who did not complete a long-term follow-up... had been confirmed as daily smokers at the 12-month follow-up. Thus, for these three individuals, carbon monoxide, urine cotinine, and TLFB self-reported daily smoking data for the long-term follow-up were imputed using their individual 12-month follow-up values.' All 15 enrolled participants are therefore analyzed (with imputation for the 3 non-completers), so N=15 is the correct denominator for the 9/15 (60%) long-term Outcome, not the 12 who physically returned.
article.Followup in months: The long-term follow-up is reported as 'mean 30 months (range = 16-57 months)' post-target-quit-date (TQD, i.e., first psilocybin session); coded as 30. Two nuances: (1) the range shows some individuals were followed to 57 months, but this reflects variable retrospective-interview scheduling around one nominal 'long-term follow-up' visit rather than a distinct longer protocol timepoint, so the mean (30) rather than the max (57) was used. (2) The rule specifies measuring from end of treatment when both an end-of-treatment and from-baseline horizon are given; Methods explicitly defines 'end of treatment (10 weeks post-TQD)' as a separate reference point, so the 30-month figure (measured from TQD, i.e., first dosing, not from the 10-week end of treatment) is very slightly longer (~2 months) than a strict end-of-treatment measurement would give; this difference does not change month-level reporting materially and was not subtracted out.
article.Retention (%): Not randomized, so denominator is enrolled N=15. At the article's longest/primary follow-up (long-term, mean 30 months), 12/15 (80%) returned and provided data; the earlier 12-month follow-up had 100% (15/15) completion. Retention (%) is coded 80, matching the long-term timepoint used for Outcome. This value sits exactly at the near-80 threshold flagged as flipping a downstream cell, so it is called out explicitly here: 12/15=80% at long-term follow-up (Abstract/Results); 15/15=100% at 12-month follow-up.
article.InclusionExclusionCriteria: This article states only one explicit exclusion criterion of its own ('without histories of severe mental illness') plus baseline descriptive characteristics (age, CPD, years smoking, prior quit attempts); it does not restate a full inclusion/exclusion list and explicitly defers: 'For a detailed description of the study sample and intervention see Johnson et al. (4).' Coded 0 for lack of a clear/complete statement within this article itself; consistent with 'eligibility'=N in the MethodologyDescribedYN criteria below.
article.BaseStatus: No formal nicotine-dependence severity instrument (e.g., FTND) is reported in this article. Coded 'Moderate' based on the described smoking history — 19 CPD, mean 31 years of smoking, mean 6 prior quit attempts (Methods) — which reflects a substantial but not explicitly 'severe'-labeled dependence profile; this is a judgment call in the absence of a validated severity score in this article.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Race/ethnicity is not reported anywhere in this article (unlike some companion articles on the same cohort); coded '.' as not reported.
article.Power: No power calculation or explicit 'underpowered' statement appears. Discussion states findings 'are limited by the small sample, open-label design, and lack of control condition' — a general small-sample limitation, not an explicit power discussion — so coded 0 (not counted as a bare underpowered statement).
article.QualityOfLifeMeasured: The Persisting Effects Questionnaire includes one single global item, 'Did the experience change your sense of well-being or life satisfaction?' (Table 1), which is adjacent to but not a dedicated/validated quality-of-life instrument (e.g., no SF-36/WHOQOL-type measure is used). Coded 0 as a judgment call; this single item could alternately support a 1.
article.RelapseMeasured: Coded 1 because the article distinguishes 'confirmed as smoking abstinent' from 'reporting continuous abstinence since their TQD' (e.g., '10 participants (67%) were confirmed as smoking abstinent, with 8 of these participants reporting continuous abstinence since their TQD'), implying explicit tracking of relapse-and-requit versus uninterrupted abstinence, and the imputation rule for non-completers treats missed follow-up as presumed relapse to smoking.
article.HarmsAssessed: Coded 1 / SafetyReported='Y' based on this article's own Results content: 'no clinically significant psychological sequelae were spontaneously reported at the long-term follow-up' and the detailed account of one participant's decreased well-being/counseling referral (Results). The acute physiological AE data recapped in the Introduction (mild headache, BP/HR elevation, 40% challenging experiences) is explicitly attributed to the previously published parent trial ('Pilot results demonstrated safety and feasibility in this sample... (4)') and is background context, not new data collected or re-analyzed in this article; it was therefore not treated as this article's own ae_events to avoid conflating the two articles' safety data, per instructions to extract only this article's evidence.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: objective: clearly stated ('To assess long-term effects of a psilocybin-facilitated smoking cessation program at >=12 months...'). design: open-label pilot follow-up described. setting: Johns Hopkins Medicine / laboratory visits stated. eligibility=N: only one exclusion criterion ('without histories of severe mental illness') plus descriptive characteristics given; full criteria explicitly deferred to ref (4). intervention: dosing/timing/CBT fully described. comparator=Y: its absence is explicitly stated as a limitation ('lack of control condition'), which counts as described-as-absent. sample_size_power=N: N=15 is stated but no power calculation or explicit underpowered statement appears, only a general 'small sample' limitation. randomization=N: the word/concept of randomization for this study's own design is never addressed (only used later regarding the planned future RCT, NCT01943994); its absence is not itself stated the way blinding's absence is. blinding=Y: 'open-label design' is explicitly named as a limitation, describing absence of blinding. statistical_methods, results, harms, funding_coi: all clearly described (Data analysis section; Results; psychological-sequelae statement; Funding/Declaration of interest sections). n_met=11 < 13, so MethodologyDescribedYN=0.

ae_events.Johnson 2016_AE01: Results: 'one participant deviated from instrument instructions by endorsing both -3 (decreased very much) and +3 (increased very much) at the 12-month follow-up... The participant endorsing mixed results for well-being or life-satisfaction at the 12-month follow-up attributed the decrease in well-being or life-satisfaction to psilocybin session content in which she reported re-experiencing traumatic childhood memories. This individual was referred to additional counseling, which she reported to be helpful in integrating these experiences and resolving associated difficulty.' AE_type='both' because the precipitating content (re-experiencing trauma) occurred in-session (challenging-experience phenomenology) but the reported effect (decreased well-being/life satisfaction) persisted to the 12-month assessment and required a counseling referral, i.e., both an in-session challenging-experience component and a clinically actionable aftermath. Onset='delayed' because the adverse rating (decreased well-being) is documented as persisting to the 12-month follow-up rather than resolving acutely. Severity='Moderate' (rubric): required active, non-pharmacological intervention (counseling referral) and involved functional/psychological impact persisting well beyond the dosing day, but meets no FDA seriousness criterion (no hospitalization, no life-threatening event, no stated suicidality). SeverityIndeterminate='N' because sufficient detail (intervention required, persistence to 12 months, described resolution via counseling) supports a confident Moderate grade. InterventionRequired='Y' (referred to additional counseling). MeetsFDASerious='N'. A second participant 'sought outside counseling after their psilocybin session experiences, although this was reportedly undertaken with the intention of personal growth and self-improvement' (Results) was considered but NOT coded as a separate AE, since the article explicitly frames it as proactive/non-distress-motivated rather than an adverse reaction. NumDistinctAEs=1, NParticipantsWithAE=1, AE_denominator=15 (all 15 completed the 12-month follow-up at which this item was assessed); ArmScope='psychedelic_arm' (single-arm study, entire sample exposed).

config_proposal.note: Single-arm, open-label long-term follow-up report with no control group and no test statistic or p-value paired with the long-term (or 12-month) abstinence rate, so none of the seven supported conversions (d, g, eta_p, F, chi2, OR, RR) apply.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: 60% (9/15) biologically verified (CO + cotinine + TLFB) smoking abstinence at long-term follow-up (mean 30 months post-TQD, range 16-57 months) in an open-label, single-arm design, contrasted by the authors against <31% typical 12-month abstinence for standard smoking-cessation medications (Discussion).
